final.memo:
The Company is currently trading as a terminal equity event, with the market pricing in a total wipeout following its May 22, 2020, Chapter 11 filing [D03], [D04]. We believe this valuation fails to account for the intrinsic value of the underlying vehicle fleet, which represents a massive, albeit mispriced, asset base [D01], [D05].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, based on a $17.5 billion estimated fleet liquidation value against $17.1 billion in total debt, suggests residual equity value potential of roughly $411 million, or $8.00 per share [D02], [D03]. This stands in stark contrast to the current $787 million market capitalization, which we view as disconnected from the potential recovery of travel demand and asset realization [D04], [D06].

The market’s myopia is driven by fear of absolute priority and the perceived permanence of the travel depression [D03], [D05]. We see a clear catalyst in the court-supervised restructuring process, where transparent asset liquidation can prove value exists above the senior debt stack [D03], [D07].

We intend to engage proactively with the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors to advocate for a reorganization plan that avoids excessive administrative dilution [D01], [D03]. We will utilize the Chapter 11 framework to monitor the creditor waterfall and ensure that any value captured from the fleet is not entirely diverted from equity holders [D03], [D05].

The primary risk is the absolute priority rule, which could render our common equity stake worthless if liquidation values fail to clear the debt stack [D05]. To protect the portfolio, we are sizing this at 2% of NAV and utilizing index puts to hedge our travel-sector beta, remaining ready to pivot to the senior debt if the equity thesis is subordinated [D08], [D05].
